findings.interpretation: Retained peer632 uses one llama_context and one batch, llama_decode then explicit llama_synchronize, all per-member GPU greedy/sample checks and head publication, then advances to the next episode/wave. Its current NVTX variant preserves those exact decode/sync/sample/publication statements. No next episode is prepared/submitted while this one is in flight in these consumers. Native implementation can still have internal asynchronous work; explicit synchronize makes that complete before the outer episode advances.

findings.claim: Single-slot serialization is already proven to be the direct current B2 performance bottleneck
findings.interpretation: It is a real architectural concurrency limit for independent future episodes, but both matched consumers serialize these dependent steps. Source existence does not allocate the measured excess host wall to this choice. A direct-cause claim needs current off-CPU/on-CPU critical-path evidence or an equal-work end-to-end candidate. Actual profiling is owned by Root.

dependencies_and_opportunity: Autoregressive natural decode of a session depends on the previous sampled token and committed recurrent/KV state. The teacher-forced B2 tape knows future token IDs, but the next step still consumes preceding recurrent/KV results. A second slot cannot remove these mathematical dependencies.

Independent sessions already share a true R2 episode. Overlapping CPU preparation of independent next episodes or different ready buckets may be an opportunity if the measured critical path warrants it, but requires separating the currently shared input/output/workspace ownership and preserving original state publication, cancellation, completion and native retirement. It is not established here as a required change or a speed gain.

A one-slot carrier is not evidence that Compute/Graph cannot support multiple invocations or that every current/future model consumer uses the same strategy. This review deliberately does not generalize to those claims.
